successors.name: Carthage
successors.text: 'the whole area between the Platani and the Salso', read as the province of Agrigento (2,782 km2 against the page's 'around 3,500 km2' under Theron)

ledger.x: c. 582: Greek colonists from Gela found Akragas. 'it was founded around 582-580 BC by Greek colonists from Gela in eastern Sicily'; further colonists from Crete and Rhodes; founders Aristonous and Pystilus. The land (Agrigento) is a reading.

c. 570: Phalaris takes the city. 'Around 570 BC, the city came under the control of Phalaris, a semi-legendary figure'; 'He ruled until around 550 BC'. His territorial campaigns are 'probably anachronistic' on the page.

c. 500: Akragas conquers Heraclea Minoa and holds the land between the Platani and the Salso. Acragas 'expanded westwards over the course of the sixth century BC. It conquered Heraclea Minoa around 500 BC'; the area 'expanded to comprise the whole area between the Platani and the Salso'. The page does not name the…
c. 488: Theron makes himself tyrant. 'Theron made himself tyrant of Acragas around 488 BC'; Thrasydaeus 'succeeded him in 472 BC'.
c. 483: Theron conquers Himera. 'Around 483 BC, Theron invaded and conquered Himera, Acragas' neighbour to the north'.
472: Theron dies and Himera slips away.

wars.name: Battle of Himera (480 BC)
wars.outcome: 'The Carthaginians invaded in 480 BC, the first of the Greco-Punic Wars, but they were defeated' by Theron and Gelon; the victory left Theron 'in the undisputed possession of the sovereignty of Himera'.

wars.name: Carthaginian invasion of 409-406 BC
wars.outcome: Himera was 'utterly destroyed' in 409; Akragas was 'captured and sacked by Carthaginian forces' in 406.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the Platani and the Salso are the rivers of its peak territory.
